Ben —

I’ll take cadence and copy. A few suggestions after a quick pass:
- Segment list: focus on "platform engineers" + "ML infra" tags; separate the invite lines so the 72h message is more technical (benchmarks, code snippets, reproducibility checklist) and the 24h message is lighter (calendar + what to bring).
- Add an RSVP path specifically for "hands-on seat required" to cap cohort at 80 per session; we'll auto-fulfill waitlist joiners with the on-demand recording + follow-up demo slot.
- For the failover link: instead of exposing a HubSpot form immediately, present a lightweight hosted landing page that preserves utm_partner & campaign params and queues registrations in a lightweight DB then posts to HubSpot once systems are healthy. That avoids double-registrations if redirects flap.

Copy tweaks (72h) — excerpt:
"In this session, we’ll deep-dive into cost-aware batching, prefix cache patterns, and practical routing rules that cut per-token spend without breaking latency SLOs. Bring one prompt and one metric you care about — we’ll instrument it live."

I’ll assemble the final cadence doc and share the spreadsheet with the tracking link map. PrIyom — if you can confirm the lightweight queue approach is feasible, I’ll lock the copy. Vivek — can you chase Acme for the HubSpot campaign id? I’ve cc’d devops for TTL suggestions in the ops spreadsheet.

Marissa

- DNS/TTL: recommending a 60s TTL on the partner redirect record for the Oct push window so we can flip quickly if we see degradation. Ops approved.
- Test plan: I’ll run the staged invite to devs@redwood.internal tomorrow 09/25 10:00 PT and post results to the shared spreadsheet.
